lead.headline: Israel votes today in a near dead heat between Netanyahu and Eisenkot, and neither bloc is forecast to reach 61 seats
lead.short: Israelis are voting in what many call the most consequential election in the country's history. Friday's final polls put Benjamin Netanyahu almost level with Gadi Eisenkot, the former army chief, and neither bloc is projected to win the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-seat Knesset, so weeks or months of coalition talks may follow.

why.text: Whoever governs Israel decides whether the war with Iran resumes, and with it the price of the oil India buys.

more: The opposition has hammered Netanyahu over the security failure that led to the 7 October 2023 attacks, in which nearly 1,200 people were killed and 251 taken hostage, and wants an independent inquiry he has long resisted. Netanyahu presents himself as "Mr Security", pointing to Israel's wars across the region and his closeness to Donald Trump.

Eisenkot's new Yashar party leads a "change bloc" that includes the right-wingers Naftali Bennett and Avigdor Lieberman and the left-leaning former general Yair Golan. Netanyahu, first prime minister in 1996, needs the far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties again. About a fifth of Israelis are Arab citizens, and two Arab blocs are running.

update.new: Polls are open; neither bloc is forecast to reach a majority.
update.front: Voting day itself, with the final polls showing no bloc near a majority.

seconds.headline: Anthropic files for a stock market listing that could value it at about $1.5 trillion, and Indian IT shares fall
seconds.short: Anthropic, the maker of Claude, has filed for a share sale under the ticker ANT that could value it at around $1.5 trillion. Its filing shows third-quarter revenue up 45% on the previous quarter to $16.8bn. TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech and Tech Mahindra fell up to 3% on Tuesday as investors weighed what AI means for their business.

why.text: India's IT companies sell the coding and back-office work that Claude now automates, and investors are pricing that in.

more: The filing shows a net loss of about $42bn in 2025, including an accounting charge of about $34bn on financing instruments that could convert into shares, Reuters reports. Excluding those write-downs, Anthropic's operating loss was more than $8bn. The loss comes from heavy spending on computing, research and staff. It reported adjusted profitability for the third quarter.

Some investors had discussed a valuation of around $2 trillion before expectations moderated. The number of shares on offer is not yet set. Overnight Nvidia rose 3%, and South Korea's Kospi jumped 5%, with SK Hynix up more than 8%. Broadcom has separately lined up $63bn from banks to finance chips for Anthropic, Bloomberg reports.

update.new: Anthropic has filed, and its accounts are public for the first time.
update.front: The filing puts real numbers on the AI boom for the first time, and moved Indian IT shares on Tuesday.

seconds.headline: Harry Kane wins the Ballon d'Or, the first Englishman in 25 years, and Alexia Putellas takes the women's award
seconds.byline: BBC · THE TIMES OF INDIA · ESPN · 27 OCT
seconds.short: Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or in London on Monday after scoring 73 goals for Bayern Munich and England, finishing ahead of Lamine Yamal, Kylian Mbappé and Lionel Messi. He is the first English winner in 25 years, since Michael Owen in 2001, and only the fifth ever. Alexia Putellas won the women's award for a third time.

why.text: Kane has spent a career being called the best player never to win anything big; this is the biggest individual prize there is.

more: Before Owen, Kevin Keegan won twice, Bobby Charlton won in 1966 and Stanley Matthews took the first prize in 1956. Kane, England's captain, set new scoring records in Germany last season. Putellas, now at London City Lionesses, beat her former Barcelona teammates Ewa Pajor and Patri Guijarro.

Virat Kohli posted a message for his "friend" on Tuesday. "Harry my friend, you deserve every bit of this award for your resilience, hard work and honesty with which you've carried yourself through all these years playing football at the top," he wrote. Kohli next plays in the five ODIs in New Zealand from 4 November.

update.new: Kane won; Putellas took the women's award.
update.front: The result: football's top individual prize goes to an Englishman for the first time since 2001.

seconds.headline: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees as it cuts costs in the age of AI
seconds.short: Microsoft will offer buyouts to about 60,000 employees, Bloomberg reported on Monday, including staff in Xbox, Windows and its Copilot AI tool, as it cuts costs while spending heavily on AI. Staff in cybersecurity, data centres and marketing are not eligible. Microsoft employs about 223,000 people worldwide. In April it offered early retirement to about 7% of its US staff.

why.text: When the biggest software company thins its own ranks for AI, the pressure on India's tech workforce is not far behind.

more: "This offer gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company a new choice to make that transition now with support," said Amy Coleman, Microsoft's chief people officer. The company gave no further details.

Meta said in April it would cut about 8,000 jobs, 10% of its staff, Amazon has made several rounds of cuts, and Oracle shed 21,000 jobs in June, all citing AI. It is unclear whether the cuts have made the companies more efficient, and some, including Meta, have scaled back their plans. A National Bureau of Economic Research survey found 90% of 9,000 senior executives said AI had not yet raised productivity at their companies.

seconds.headline: India says new permanent Security Council members without a veto would be 'second-class', and the veto must be shared by all
seconds.short: India's ambassador to the UN, Harish Parvathaneni, said on Monday that any reform creating permanent members without veto powers would relegate them to "second-class" status and leave the existing five in control. "As long as the veto exists, it must be held by all permanent members," he said, calling India's position principled and well known.

why.text: India has spent decades seeking a permanent seat, and this sets out what it will and will not accept.

more: China, France, Russia, Britain and the US are the permanent members of the 15-member Council and hold vetoes; the other ten members are elected for two years at a time. Parvathaneni said fairness and justice demanded equal rights and responsibilities for all permanent members of a reformed Council.

Russia's foreign minister Sergey Lavrov has said Moscow supports India's and Brazil's bids for permanent seats, while stressing the interests of Africa. "We are in favour of broadening the representation of Asia, Africa, and Latin America," Lavrov said. Talks on reforming the Council have run for years at the UN General Assembly without agreement on the veto.

stories.headline: Jordan strikes militants in Syria in revenge for the Karak church attack, and Syria says five civilians were killed
stories.short: Jordanian jets struck what Amman called "terrorist organisations" in a village in Syria's southern Daraa province on Monday, in retaliation for Friday's shooting at a Christian funeral that killed nine people. Syrian health officials said five people, including women, children and an elderly man, were killed. Syria said it had not been told, and closed the Nassib border crossing.

why.text: Two neighbours trying to keep their own peace are now at odds, on the edge of the wider war with Iran.

more: Jordan said it had coordinated with the Syrian government and that its jets had killed and wounded "several terrorists". Syria said it had "opened direct channels of communication" with Jordanian officials and launched investigations. Nassib is the only passenger and commercial crossing between the two countries, and all traffic in both directions is suspended.

Earlier on Monday, Jordanian forces arrested two brothers and their brother-in-law, hiding in an abandoned house in Karak, over the church attack. Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya said the attackers were all Jordanians. Nine people were killed and 34 injured at the Greek Orthodox church on Friday.

update.new: Jordan struck in Syria; Syria closed the border.

stories.headline: Jio Platforms lists on Wednesday, and a grey-market premium of 22% would make it India's second most valuable company
stories.short: Jio Platforms makes its stock market debut on Wednesday, and a 22% grey-market premium points to a value of about ₹12.5 lakh crore, which would put it ahead of Bharti Airtel and behind only its parent, Reliance Industries. At the top of its price band Jio is valued at about ₹10.3 lakh crore. Grey-market prices are unofficial.

why.text: It was India's biggest share sale, and how it trades will shape every large listing that follows.

more: The issue, of about ₹30,200 crore, was the largest in Indian history. It was fully subscribed within 100 minutes and drew more than 1.38 crore applications, more than any IPO anywhere, with cumulative demand above ₹7 lakh crore. By the close it was subscribed 22.2 times, and the portion for institutions 70.55 times.

A listing gain of about 15% would be enough to pass Airtel, worth ₹12.25 lakh crore. Reliance is worth ₹16.12 lakh crore. Jio would be the strongest debut by a newly listed Indian company by market value. On Tuesday the Sensex was down 0.3% at 2pm, with Infosys falling again and Tata Consumer up about 6% after its results.

update.new: The listing is on Wednesday, and the grey market points to a big debut.

briefs.headline: Gold slips to about $4,005 an ounce ahead of Wednesday's Fed decision, as traders bet on a rate rise by December
briefs.text: Spot gold fell 0.3% to about $4,005 as the dollar held near a two-week high. Traders see an 11% chance of a Fed rate rise this week and 80% by December, and silver slid 2.1% to $52.77.

notes.Sensex: Down 0.3% at 73,371 at 2pm, after rising 500 points from the day's low in the morning.

notes.Nasdaq-100: Rose 1.1% on Monday and the S&P 500 0.7%, led by AI shares.

stories.headline: OpenAI says its models have proved a central conjecture in harmonic analysis and made two more discoveries
stories.short: OpenAI said on Monday that its AI models proved the local smoothing conjecture, a central problem in harmonic analysis, in every spatial dimension; mathematicians had proved it only in three. It also says they disproved the Exponential Time Hypothesis in computer science and gave a rigorous proof of the existence of quantum chromodynamics, the theory of quarks and gluons.

why.text: If the claims hold up, they are the strongest sign yet that AI can do original mathematics, not just check it.

more: "Now I am filled with joy and optimism, because the scientific enterprise as a whole is going to make giant leaps as a result of the AI revolution," said Alex Iosevich, a mathematics professor who worked on the findings. He expects theoretical mathematics to "change drastically".

OpenAI says it has reached out to scientists outside the company to turn its "raw research data into scientific understanding", and chose different ways of releasing each finding after consulting them. Researchers had previously proved the local smoothing conjecture only in three dimensions. The claims still need checking by other mathematicians and physicists, as earlier breakthroughs credited to AI have.
